Incremented by $B859 in the raster handler. The foreground waits for a change when synchronizing screen updates.

Transfer entry for reset title sequence at $391F. Preserves the caller registers and stack across the JMP.
Transfer entry for stop title sequence at $3953. Preserves the caller registers and stack across the JMP.
Transfer entry for tick title sequence at $3959. Preserves the caller registers and stack across the JMP.
Pitch offsets, three countdowns, three stream indices and sequence state for the title player. $3911 gates sequencing and $3912 supplies the first voice's current descriptor.
Resets the three duration counters, sequence indices and embedded source pointers for the title tune sequencer.
Clears $3911, the flag tested by the title loop before processing the sequence.
Steps each voice's duration counter, reads a pitch and duration when it expires, loops its stream on $FF and sends notes to $F006. Voice 0 also interprets instrument changes and a rest command.
Pitch and duration pairs for voice 1. The first byte of a pair can also request an instrument or rest. $FF in pitch position loops to the start.
Pitch and duration pairs for voice 2. The sequencer adds the offset in $390A to each pitch and restarts this stream on $FF.
Eight pitch and duration pairs for the third voice, followed by the $FF loop byte.
Source sprite records 0 to 15 for the mirroring pass. Each record occupies 64 bytes including one padding byte.
Source sprite records 16 to 31. Each group of three bytes holds the next row of one 24-by-21 shape.
Source frames 32 to 47. The mirroring pass alternates the multicolour and single-bit byte-reversal tables between the two records of a pair.
Source frames 48 to 63 in the two-record layout read by $AD21.
The final ten source records read by $ACE5. The next range beginning at $5280 is a destination for generated or copied frames.
First sixteen slots of the sprite frame buffer. Title, message and play setup choose which patterns occupy it.
Sprite buffer records 16 to 31, copied from $E400 in the base setup and rewritten when mirrored frames are prepared.
Sprite buffer records 32 to 47, copied from $E800 in the base setup.
Sprite buffer records 48 to 63. The load at $B44B ends at $627F. The mirroring loop can continue past that point.
Final ten destination records of the 74-frame mirroring pass from $ACE5.
Eight 64-byte sprite slots for pointers $94-$9B in VIC bank $4000. Includes the blank frame $9A used to hide objects.
Scratch page cleared by $BCEF during player sprite initialization.
First 128 eight-byte patterns of the character set selected by $B893 for the top of the display.
Final 128 patterns selected by the same $6800 VIC character-set base.
Enters the C64 build through $8017. The immediate byte at $8001 is also read as the platform selector by memory banking and VIC initialization.
The immediate operand of the C64 entry stub is also the flag read by the code supporting two banking paths.
Powers of two from $01 to $80. Code can select a single bit by index.
Complements of the eight masks at $8005, indexed in the same bit order.
Configures the processor port when the platform byte is set, initializes the engine and SID, sets the one-player and sound flags, then enters the title setup at $803E.
Resets the stack to $FE, clears the byte at $170A and runs the title-screen setup before entering the game selection loop.
Calls the selection handler at $842E and restarts the title setup on carry clear.
Clears the active player's tower bonus counters, clears the interlude mode flag and preserves the progress mask before returning to tower setup.
Saves the player's position and view around the finish bonus panel, then prepares the collapse scene and resumes the saved positions.
When the startup guard at $8015 is clear, reads play-time keyboard commands including the shortcut that returns to title, setting or clearing flags at $1709-$170A.
Generates display character data, decodes the tower selected by $4A and initializes player, object, shot, and pending floor state.
Restores the character-set backup and initializes the scrolling background, sprite frames, submarine, fish slots and screen before the interlude.
Polls joystick and updates player, destructible tiles, projectiles and objects. Builds a back buffer, waits for display synchronization, swaps buffers and refreshes object sprites.
Compares the current height to the previous awarded watermark and advances the watermark while adding $10 of BCD score per step.
Polls the stick, updates the submarine and fish slots, draws the background, waits for the raster tick and swaps screen pages before sprite and contact updates.
Sets both saved tower indices from $8016 and gives both players the full eight-bit tower mask.
Chooses the live player for this turn, restoring their tower index and eight separate tower flags. Carry clear returns to the title when neither eligible player has a nonzero tower mask.
Packs the eight per-tower flags in $DC-$E3 into the current player's mask and saves the tower index along with the sign flag from $1704.
Zeros the current player's tower mask in $841A indexed by $51.
Clears the current tower's flag and advances the tower index in $4A and the current player's saved index.
Zero-terminated message records for the intro, tower names, results, credits, sound and player options. Values $01-$0F within a record select text colour.
Printable part of the PLAYER ONE record, following its colour control byte.
Name record for the first tower, read through the first pointer at $86BE.
Name record for tower 2.
Name record for tower 3.
Name record for tower 4.
Name record for tower 5.
Name record for tower 6.
Name record for tower 7.
The final tower name, EDGE OF DOOM, followed by the two lines introducing the fish bonus.
Offset into the NO LIVES LEFT message record. The following strings describe completion and its bonus.
Start of the technique line in the tower-completion panel.
Updatable numeric cells near the end of the technique line and the start of the extras row.
Tail of the EXTRAS row and part of the mission success and credit text block.
Eight little-endian pointers to the names that appear when entering a tower, indexed by twice the tower number.
First high pointer byte in the little-endian table of tower names.
X coordinates for the eight tower preview icons, written to the eight VIC sprite position registers.
Draws the entering message and the selected tower name, updates the player legend and sets eight sprites for the tower preview before waiting.
Displays the game over and lives message for the current player, with its associated effects and delay.
Prepares the message scene, plays the time-out sound sequence, writes the active player and TIME LIMIT UP, then waits.
Draws the congratulations and mission completed messages and tries to enter initials after the timed display.
Draws the active player legend and the two centered lines introducing the fish bonus scene, then waits for a raster or joystick transition through $8B51.
Draws the completion panel, subtracts the remaining timer and then other bonus counters in BCD steps, and awards score as it updates each displayed value.
Converts the remaining time and the two player-selected bonus counters to decimal characters in the three result messages and requests a pitch derived from the bonus state.
Prepares two title sprites from data at $EE00 and $EF00, alternates the title and score views using the counter at $89BE, reads player and sound options through the keyboard matrix and exits on fire.
Draws the one-player or two-player option then the sound on or sound off option according to $50 and $67.
Eight X coordinates for the sprite strip drawn by $8AFF.
Assigns sprite pointers $4A-$51 to both screen pages and positions eight sprites using $8AF6 and their common Y at $8AFE.
Resets the SID, initializes a black display, clears the scene-dependent display state and refreshes status graphics for a message.
Waits for the raster tick, swaps screen pages and then enters the timed message wait with the original A value.
Uses A as a count of display ticks. A fresh fire press ends the wait early after release.
Polls the stick until the decoded fire byte $26 is zero.
Selects the message pointer using the active player at $51 before drawing it.
Draws the high-score heading and sends the table's rows to $8C67.
Acts on a score admitted by $8CB9. Initializes the initials to A and two spaces, cycles a letter with signed vertical input, and confirms each letter with fire.
Sets the text position and colour and prints the selected record's packed score digits and initials through the two-cell writer.
Draws each half of A as a decimal glyph by adding ASCII zero before calling the text routine.
Masks to a single digit and maps it to the selected character pair through $A987.
Compares the selected player's score to the high-score records and returns the entry pointer if the score qualifies.
Starts the player at angle 4 and height 8, derives the view height, sets the facing bit and resets action, leave-scene and input state.
Adds the motion delta to the player angle and uses the geometry probe to reject collisions.
Adds the signed delta in A to the 10-bit height at $C7-$C8. If the collision check sets carry it restores the old height. A negative high byte exits through $93E4.
Calls the directional support test and applies its delta only if the player supplies no horizontal input.
Dispatch destinations stored minus one. The routine at $8DD4 pushes high then low from the indexed pair, so RTS adds one and enters the selected handler.
High byte of the first biased return address in the player-state dispatch table.
In the eligible mode, suppresses a held fire press after its first poll using $27. Selects a handler by pushing the return address encoded at $8DC0 for state $CD.
Clears $CD and its phase counter $CC, returning the dispatcher to state 0.

Tests geometry under the player, then chooses a state for the detected surface. In the ordinary branch, direction and fire initiate a jump while fire without direction initiates the shot. Vertical input can try lift or doorway code.
Sets player state 3 and clears its animation phase. The handler at $8E9E completes seven frames and reverses the facing bit in $CB.
Selects one of two 7-entry sequences from $9021 by facing, updates $CE, and flips the facing bit after the seventh step.
Starts the stationary variant of state 2. Nearby entries choose the signed push direction and animation before sharing the stores at $8EF2.
Advances state 2 with its working counter and the motion parameters selected by the entry path at $8EC3-$8EF2.
Sets state 1, captures the stick direction at $8F79, resets the jump phase and its working values, and requests effect 9.
Runs the jump using its phase counter and the direction saved by $8F90. Checks vertical and horizontal motion as it progresses.
Enters state 4, clears its phase and $9052, and requests effect 7.

During phases 0 to 3, attempts a one-unit step toward the center of the angular cell, but advances the animation even if geometry rejects the step. Later phases hide and reveal the player. The test at $9125 requires $170B to equal 3 for the collapse path.
Hides the player once the doorway animation reaches phase $0D. A summit flag starts a timed pause that signals completion. The regular route moves the hidden player around the tower before emerging.
Uses the reversed phase count and facing to select a frame from the paired opening animation tables.
Immediate operand used when selecting the reverse doorway animation frame.
Enters state 5 only if the shot slot at $9B contains $FF, then resets the animation phase and requests sound $0F.
Sets the sprite frame from $904B and the facing bit. On animation phase 1 it initializes the projectile before resetting the state after phase 3.
Copies player height into the shot slot, chooses the initial angle one step to either side of $C6, marks the slot active and records its signed direction from the facing bit.
Saves the requested vertical direction, enters state 6 with its phase reset and releases a matching pending floor change through $B13F.
Centers the player in the current angular cell before updating the lift and player height through the selected direction.
Attempts a collision against the four slots using the player's current angle and height, then checks special states and relative height before returning.
Checks the visible player against the object slots and adjusts motion or changes player state when the contact path wins.
Enters player state 7, clears its phase and result flag, subtracts two technique points and requests sound $0B.
Sixteen signed height increments for early falling phases. The handler at $93AB caps its lookup at index 15.

Selects a facing-relative animation frame and adds the signed vertical displacement at $9380. After the initial phase it moves downward in four-unit steps and checks for landing or crossing zero height.
Sets state 8 and zero height, changes or clears active object slots, resets sound and queues effects $0C and $0D.
Steps the phase counter and selects a sprite frame from its quarter speed value for the first $18 phases.
Sets state 9, seeds the phase counter with $FF and resets the SID before collapse updates.
In the descending phase, lowers the player and shifts each of the sixteen map columns down a tile beginning near the visible height. The six-row threshold chooses the last collapse phase.
Eight colour registers initialized at $9575 during the collapse animation.
Restores base sprite shapes, positions eight debris sprites and advances their X and Y spread with display ticks while queuing successive collapse effects.
Marks the projectile slot as free and clears its render state.
Indexed increments added to the projectile height during its active movement phases.

Advances the shot along the circumference, applies its height-change table and tests the scenery and object slots. Changes the struck slot or starts the projectile's ending phase according to the result.
Clears the four type bytes at $9C-$9F so those shared object slots begin inactive.

Derives the draw height at $68-$69 from $45-$46 minus eight and the threshold at $6A-$6B from $45-$46 plus $4D. Applies a wrap correction to the lower coordinate before updating object visibility and order.
Passes the four main object slots and a fifth slot to $A9B7. The fifth gets the blank pointer $9A when its phase is $FF.
Compares the four projected object positions to build a six-bit ordering index for assigning sprite slots.
Four entries select the alternating colour during an object's short timed colour animation.

Visits slots 3 down to 0 by $9C type. Type 7 animates and moves along the circumference. Type 5 times a transition to type 2. Other active slots check geometry and update movement before the shared next-slot tail.
Advances the current object's vertical or contact state, checking the map and the other slots before selecting a new phase.
Continues the height update with wrap and collision recovery. The following paths can restore the old coordinates and change slot state or chase direction.
Tests a candidate object's angular distance and height against the active object slots, reporting a matching slot in X when the overlap checks pass.
Tests the candidate slot against one of two class mask tables and returns the matching pair, or continues the earlier search.
Builds a probe from the object's signed motion and current position. Uses the return value to select the advance, reverse or fall path.
Sixteen computed column offsets refreshed each draw from $9CDC and the current player angle.
Projects sixteen angular columns, then compares each slot's height to the drawing bounds. Hides or retires out-of-range slots and passes visible slots to $9DBA.
Wraps the supplied angle after adding $20 and subtracting the player's angle $C6. Returns the 0-to-127 index in X and its projected value from $C980 in A.
Maps the angular difference from the player into the folded depth value used for sprite ordering.
First byte of the three-byte mask contribution for each relative tower column.
Second mask byte merged when an object draws behind the edge of a tile.
Third mask byte for the same occlusion class selected at $9F99.
Maps a projected X column to the initial three-byte mask index. $FF values reject the column.
Converts both nybbles of the object's width and alignment byte into angular bounds, iterates columns with a 16-column wrap, and uses carry to report special states or a rendered overlay.
Patched high address from the frame pointer table for the first sprite-mask write.
High byte of the address patched for the next mask write.
High byte of the address patched for the third mask row write.
Maps the current angular column to a relative screen column, clips outside 0 through 26 and calls $9F72 for two or three successive map rows using three source-plane offsets.
Patched immediate that saves the projected column index for the remaining mask calls on the current tile.
Reads a map tile, selects a mask class by sign and low bits and intersects three mask bytes in the selected row of the object buffer.
Class lookup for ordinary solid map cells, indexed by relative display column. Negative values suppress the contribution.
Matching column lookup when the tile's bits 2 and 3 select a different shape.
Column lookup selected when the eligible tile has bit 0 clear.
Continuation of the third occlusion class lookup across the $A000 ledger boundary.
Generates repeated character-code strips in RAM pages beginning at $0200 to serve as source patterns for the submarine scene's background.
Takes three random bits and uses them to select a background character from $A0E8.
Eight character codes indexed by the low three random bits.
Selects the offscreen page in the following row writer's absolute store operands. Splits each of four scrolling coordinates into a fine phase and a coarse source index.
Fills 20 columns of the back buffer using the source rows at $0200-$0900. The patched load addresses advance the four pattern layers independently.
Patched low byte of the first source load. The row loop decrements it for the next row.
Patched high byte of the last absolute store in the twenty-column underwater row writer.
When $D1 is set, adds offsets 0 through 3 to the four layer coordinates and masks each high byte to three bits.
Waits for the raster high bit to rise and fall, copies eight pages of pristine patterns back from RAM under I/O to $7800, restores the line-0 vector and re-enables interrupts.
Copies four fine scroll values to shadow $D016 registers at $3F-$42 with the mode bits set, and loads the scene colour from the tower-indexed table.
Enables the eight sprites, clears expansion and priority and sets the multicolour mask. Seeds all eight buffered sprite pointers with the blank frame $9A.
Sets the sprite mode and colours and selects the group of four pointers at $3A-$3D for the submarine state. State 3 chooses its final animation frames or the blank pointer.
Sets the starting coordinates, layer-update flag and submarine animation state.
Handles fire and the vertical stick motion through scene state, adjusts submarine position, begins a bubble when allowed and advances scroll.
Marks all four slots inactive and schedules the first three fish entry timers.
Clears one slot by setting its type to $FF. Also clears the linked bubble when it targeted this slot.
Walks the fish and bubble slots, chooses the display pointer for each and sets their sprite coordinate and display state.
Initializes slot 3 with the requested X and Y, clears the phase and queues effect 4.
Consumes the inactive slots' delays, initializes an expired slot at the entry edge and derives its motion and display parameters for this tower.
Patched table operand used to select this tower's class of fish motion.
Eight rows of eight vertical rates, combined with the sign and random low bits when a fish is allocated.

Updates the four slots at $A4C1-$A4D4 by type. Fish move horizontally with a vertical bounce and are recycled when their X coordinate runs out. The fourth slot handles a bubble, including a case that follows another slot's coordinates.
When the bubble is in the active flight state, builds a rectangle around sprite 3 and tests the active fish positions. Saves a hit slot in $A4EA.
Builds two rectangles around the submarine sprite groups. Tests type-1 fish against them, then awards 25, 50, 75 or 100 points according to the absolute vertical rate at $A4E1.

Sets the CIA1 directions, maps RAM under I/O, copies eight pages from $7800 to $D000, restores I/O and clears screen and state buffers.
Disables interrupts and exposes RAM with either the processor port or $FF00 according to the platform selector.
Restores the I/O mapping through the selected platform register and enables interrupts.
Saves the current value of $1707 in A and waits until the raster interrupt changes it.
Eight bytes copied to $D4-$DB during display setup.
Clears the low VIC sprite registers, zeroes the border and primes the screen page selectors and tower colour list.
Selects colour 8 for the fill, waits for the raster tick and joins the display reset at $AADF.
Selects colour 0 for the fill, waits for the raster tick and sets $1705 before joining the display reset.
Clears video state, initializes sprite pointers and colours, fills colour RAM from index $C8 and clears both screen buffers with a swap between clears.
Zeros the screen buffer headed by page $28 from offset $00C7 through $03FF.
Exchanges the screen-buffer page bytes $28 and $29 and encodes the two pages into the high nibbles of the shadow VIC memory registers $34 and $35.
Writes $FF to CIA1 port A, combines the active-low inputs from both CIA ports and stores signed horizontal and vertical directions in $24/$25 and fire in $26.
Selects a matrix row through the mask indexed by X at $AC1A, then inverts CIA1 port B and keeps the requested bits with the mask indexed by Y at $AC12.
Offset into the table of screen row low bytes used by the tower row writer. It uses row five as its base.
Offset into the row high-byte table. The tower row writer adds the active back-page base.

Eight row-select bytes written to CIA1 port A by $ABAD.
Eight replacement bytes for the generated pattern at $7938, copied verbatim.
Sixty-four remapped pixel bytes copied to $7EB8 after the procedural character generation.
Generates 256 eight-byte patterns at $7800. Each starts with $FF and has seven remapped bytes, then the routine replaces selected glyphs from two smaller tables.
Converts each of the four pixel pairs in A and returns a packed byte. Exchanges pair values 0 and 3 and preserves values 1 and 2.
Builds byte-reversal tables, then reads 37 adjacent pairs of sprites from $4000 and writes their mirrored forms starting at $5280.
Reverses the order of the three bytes per row and remaps their pixels. Uses $1200 for the first 21 rows and $1300 for the second sprite's 21 rows.
Fills $1300 with reversed bits and $1200 with reversed two-bit groups for all 256 possible byte values.
Prepares the broadest of the three angular probe widths and joins the row collision scan at $AE28.
Sets the angle interval and probe parameters for object slot Y, then joins the common map scan at $AE28.
Selects the third set of probe bounds and offsets for object slot Y.
Upper edge compare inside the collision scan. The row processing at $AEB5 patches the immediate byte as the candidate cell changes.
Converts the two-byte vertical coordinate in X and Y into a tile row for the map pointer and returns its low address byte in A.
Reads the two cells on either side of the foot angle. Selects a support result from $AF73 using the two occupancy flags and the fine angle.
Four outcomes for each of eight fractional angles, indexed by the occupancy of the two candidate support tiles.
Computes the base map pointer for the player's current angle and height. The 0-to-15 column comes from $C6 shifted right three times, and $AF09 computes the row.
Returns carry set only for a negative map byte with low two bits equal to 3. A contains the tile's $40 flag on that path.
Points just below the player and recognizes tile bytes $85, $89 and $8D. Returns carry set and direction 1, minus 1 or 0 respectively.
Tests the cell below the player for a negative tile with low bits 1 and masked type $10. Clears a matching tile and queues effect $13.
Recognizes tile types $20 and $30 among the negative cells with low two bits 1. Returns a signed direction and carry set, or carry clear.
Three background colour values per tower, copied to $2B, $2C and $2A in that order.
The third component of the first tower palette, loaded to the background-zero shadow at $2A.
Eight high bytes of occupancy-stream pointers. Their low bytes are zero.
Selects colours and two source streams with $4A. Expands two masks per row into a column-major grid in pages $02-$11, with the row number in the low address byte. Consumes one literal per set bit.
Reads one occupancy byte low bit first. Each zero bit writes zero and each one consumes a literal tile from the other stream. Advances both source pointers as needed.
Finds a free one of four slots, saves the tile and its address, and starts a $7D tick countdown unless the original tile's mask $0C equals $04. Returns carry set on success.
Counts down the pending slots and queues sound $19 on expiry. Then replaces tiles along the row one step at a time until it reaches the $04 class, writes $85 there and frees the slot.
Scans pending slots for the tile pointer in $02-$03 and marks the matching slot free by storing $FF in its countdown.

Walks the map from its saved row and column for a free object slot, skipping the cells that lack object type bits. Converts the found type in bits 4-6 to slot data or defers a cell beyond the current height threshold.
Advances the colour index modulo eight and skips the entry matching the tower's foreground colour before storing the result in the object slot.
Reloads the source sprites, sets up multicolour, colour and position registers, and runs the opening tower sprite sequence.
Copies sixteen pages from $E000-$EFFF to the sprite storage at $5280-$627F.
Eight little-endian BCD timer decrements for retry adjustment at $B655.
High BCD byte of tower 1's retry adjustment, paired with $B46E.
Top left glyph code indexed by the displayed BCD digit.
Top right glyph code for the same digit.
Bottom left glyph code for the same digit.
Bottom right glyph code written by $B6EB.
Eight glyph codes installed in the first status label row.
Eight glyph codes installed below them by the HUD setup.
Clears the first 200 cells and colour entries of the top screen then installs player legends, fixed label glyphs and score and life display data.
Selects the active-player display marker, writes both players' life markers and refreshes the numeric scores.
Splits the score byte indexed by X into two nybbles, adds one to each to get digit tiles, and writes them at descending offsets Y.
Fills eight cells from Y in the top panel, drawing the life icon $16 while the given count remains positive.
Adds the BCD amount in X and Y to the active player's four-byte score. Awards a life on the checked score thresholds, capped at eight.
Zeros the selected player's extra-bonus field and sets the other two-byte counter to $0100.
Subtracts a BCD byte from the active player's technique counter, clamping a negative result to zero.
The immediate subtraction amount at $B607, patched from the caller's A by $B601.
Adds a BCD increment to the active player's extras counter and limits it to $0500.
Subtracts the current tower's BCD time decrement from the timer, flooring at the decrement value when the subtraction borrows.
Increments the timer divider except when it is negative, then subtracts one BCD unit at divider five and refreshes the timer digits.
The immediate subtraction operand inside the timer's BCD update.
Splits the timer bytes into decimal digit nybbles and draws them into the two rows of the fixed display.
Uses A as the digit and Y as the column offset, then writes a two-by-two glyph from the four tables at $B47E, $B488, $B492 and $B49C.
Source bytes for space, angle brackets, at sign, asterisk and zero. The next two six-byte tables choose the left and right glyph for each.

Maps A-Z to pairs starting at $36 and 1-9 to pairs starting at $6A. Controls below $10 select colour and punctuation uses the table at $B6F6. Writes two cells to the back screen and their colour RAM, then advances the text column.
The glyph-pair writer stores the incoming Y here and reloads it just before X at exit.
The glyph-pair writer stores the incoming X here before drawing and reloads it at exit.
Walks a zero-terminated message at $02-$03, calling the two-cell glyph writer for each nonzero byte and carrying into the next page as needed.
Receives the message pointer in X and Y, counts bytes at least $10, subtracts that width from column $14 and draws with the existing row and colour.
Stores X as the text column and Y as the text row.
Selects VIC bank, disables CIA timer IRQ sources, sets the RAM vectors and schedules raster line $FA.
Increments the foreground tick, dispatches sound when enabled, and selects the line-0 handler at $B88B.
Programs the top-of-screen memory and colour registers, then selects one of two line-$50 handlers according to $1705.
Changes the high screen-select nybble of $D018 in the line-80 title/interlude branch.
Applies the display state and schedules $B981 at line $5C.
Delays briefly, loads the three background colours from $2A-$2C and updates sprite pointers according to the flag in its own operand at $B99F.
Chooses the visible screen page using the patched immediate, copies pointers $36-$3D there, and schedules the next raster split according to the scene and waterline flags.
Patched immediate deciding which screen page receives the visible tower sprite pointers.
Schedules the scene-specific split, the waterline split, or line $FA when neither early split is needed, then updates the timer before interrupt return.
Changes the three backgrounds from $2D-$2F, replaces the eight visible sprite pointers with $9A and schedules the line-250 handler.
Patched immediate deciding which screen page has its sprite pointers cleared in the waterline split.
Sets the first interlude band colour and fine horizontal scroll, then programs the line-143 handler.
Changes the foreground band's colour and horizontal scroll, then schedules line 158.
Loads the next horizontal scroll and sets the next split at line 166.
Changes the two multicolour backgrounds and schedules raster 174.
Applies the next horizontal scroll and schedules line 191.
Sets horizontal scroll and the lower background colour, then schedules line 215.
Updates lower-band scroll and repositions sprite 7 with the expansion and priority bits for the lower band. Schedules line 250.
Runs the generator at $BC5D 256 times to fill the page at $1600 and resets the self-modified read address at $BCA8.
Returns the next byte in the pool and advances its patched low address operand, wrapping inside page $16.
Fixed high operand byte of the read from $1600. The stream advances its low byte at $BCAB.
When A is nonzero, consumes a pool byte and repeatedly subtracts A to return the remainder.
Configures the VIC sprite masks and the player pair colours, clears the page at $6700 and builds 256 two-byte sprite-frame pointers at $1400 and $1500.
Derives two adjacent sprite pointers from the player's frame and facing. Positions both sprites at the same coordinate, with a third sprite below when the support frame is present.
Maps tagged object coordinates to a sprite position using the tower projection and supplies the pointer and colour used by the raster code.
Projects the 7-bit angular delta through $C980 and converts the height relative to $45 into raster Y. Returns low X, the X high bit and Y at $B3-$B5.
Restores the previously exchanged pair of pattern pages if needed. With A nonzero, chooses a new pair using the tower index modulo four.
Swaps the two pages selected by the pointer table at $BE57 with the corresponding pages at $6A00.
Sixteen angular sample offsets indexed and wrapped by the hole draw and erase loops.
Selects the offscreen row and saves the angle, row base and column start for that page. The loop inserts character $27 into blank cells based on the indexed mask.
Patched subtraction operand read by the ten-row loop, set from the current angle at $BEDB.
Restores the previous alignment saved for the back page. Erases only matching $27 cells where the mask for their row permits.
Patched subtraction operand loaded from the back page's saved angle before the erase loop.
The two hole passes index these 64 flags with a masked angular difference.
Chooses the buffer from $28 and zeros four adjacent offsets at each $14-byte stride through its unrolled stores.
Unrolled equivalent of the $BFDC loop, writing the buffer based at $7400 instead of $7000.
Computes the two water pattern offsets from the scrolling coordinates and writes them into the alternating rows of the selected back page.
Copies sixteen character bytes from the phase-selected pattern into the first ten alternating rows in the $7000 buffer.
Low source byte of the first water pattern load, patched from $C0D4.
Copies the alternate pattern into the other ten rows in the $7000 buffer.
Low source byte of the alternating pattern load for the $7000 screen.
Writes the first waterline pattern into the alternating rows in the $7400 buffer.
Low pattern byte for the first group of rows drawn to $7400.
Writes the second waterline pattern into the remaining alternating rows in the $7400 buffer.
Low pattern byte for the second group of rows drawn to $7400.

Forms the target height $C7-$C8 minus $28, computes its wrapped difference from $45-$46 and advances the view by a quarter of the low-byte magnitude rounded up, with the sign of the difference restored.
Updates $4C and writes the water surface across the bottom of the screen according to the vertical scroll position. It leaves the tower columns of the first surface row intact.
Character codes used to fill the bottom rows of the water area in the back screen.
Clears sky rows into the background buffer when the view position extends beyond the map height in $4B.
Added to the tower map column for each rendered angular phase and reduced to four bits.
Steps in the 128-unit rotation lattice for successive projected columns.

Clears the draw band and splits the vertical coordinate and rotation into fine and coarse components. The projection tables at $C800 and $C880 choose row routines by angular phase. Patches operands and call sites before drawing the rows.
High operand byte of the tile fetch at $C3F1. The projection loop patches it to the selected map column page.
High target byte of the dynamically selected outer edge row writer.
Mask bytes ANDed with the current cell before merging a one-cell edge fragment.
Bit values ORed into the current cell after preserving its other pixels.
Uses the current angle in X to select edge positions and mask controls. Writes the affected tile bytes and rejoins the projection row loop.
Four row writers patched into the first low-bit variant of the front edge dispatch.
Writes the first front-edge tile pattern into the row chosen by the angular dispatch.
Merges the first and last cell nybbles and writes $BF, $BA and $99 between them before returning to the row loop.
Clears the leading low bits, writes $6F, $EE and $A6 and merges the trailing cell with $50.
Four row writers used by the second angular edge when the tile selects the alternate branch.
Merges boundary pixels with the current row for the second-edge dispatch.
Writes $FA and merges its two adjacent edge nybbles into the existing row.
Writes $BE and adjusts its two adjacent cells with the masks $FC and $03.
Four address pairs patched into the inner edge dispatch through $C438.
Writes the first inner-edge pattern, selected by the low two bits of the projected angle.
Writes $3F, $FF and $FC in the next three cells of the current row.
Merges $0F into the leading cell, writes two $FF cells and masks the trailing edge.
Four address pairs patched into the outer writer dispatch at $C443.
Variable mask values indexed by the tile parameter in X at $C690.
Merges the indexed edge mask into the first cell of the outer edge.
Uses the current X to select the center value at $C650 and merge boundary values into nybble-aligned edge cells.
Writes the indexed center value followed by the shifted boundary fragment, preserving the lowest two bits of the trailing cell.
Indexed by angular phase in $C31B. Low two bits select a first-edge row routine, with upper bits used for a displacement or special handling.
Second projection table read by the row planner at $C3C1. Low two bits choose independent row routines for the other edge.
For the special-edge branch at $C4A6, supplies a column index with the same angular index used by the mask-control table.
Chooses single or multiple cell masks and flags for the special-edge branch at $C4AD.
Maps the 128 wrapped angles produced by $9CDC to projected coordinates.
Eight 128-byte tables selected by the fine angle at $9C49 and addressed indirectly through $16-$17. $9DBA reads the object-specific byte for its angular width and screen clipping.
Packed pixel patterns fetched by the waterline generator at $C108, $C161 and $C18D. The path at $C134 starts $40 bytes farther into the same pattern region.
Packed character values for the alternate rows written by $C134.
Last 128 bytes of the indexed $CE00 waterline pattern region. The drawing routine patches the low source byte for the current phase.
Eight pages of character and tile bytes copied from the hand-over's $7800-$7FFF with I/O banked out. This matches the source snapshot byte for byte.
Second four pages of the pattern backup restored by $A280, corresponding to the hand-over patterns at $7C00-$7FFF.
First sixteen 64-byte frames of the source block copied by $B44B. Copied to $5280-$567F.
Sprite seed frames 16 to 31 from the block restored by $B44B. Copied to $5680-$5A7F.
Sprite seed frames 32 to 47 from the block restored by $B44B. Copied to $5A80-$5E7F.
Final sixteen sprite seed frames restored to $5E80-$627F by $B44B.
Title path copies this page to $5280 as part of the 512-byte title sprite patch.
Title path copies this page to $5380 after the first page of title patterns.
Transfer entry for initialize sid at $F090. Preserves the caller registers and stack across the JMP.
Transfer entry for trigger effect any voice at $F0C0. Preserves the caller registers and stack across the JMP.
Transfer entry for tick sid voice state at $F3C6. Preserves the caller registers and stack across the JMP.
Sets SID volume to 15, clears routing and the voice control registers, and zeros voice state and sequence pointers.
Enters the sound descriptor reader with automatic voice selection and no explicit pitch override.
Converts the descriptor number in A into a 32-byte record in RAM at $F800. Chooses a voice, loads its derived state and writes the descriptor's attack and sustain bytes to SID.
Returns the index in Y, trying inactive voices from 2 down, then released voices. When all three are gated it compares their countdowns.
Reads a six-byte modulator record through the descriptor pointer at $FB-$FC, distributes the values to the X-selected state slots and clears the two counters.
Iterates six modulator slots. Decodes the low three bits of each type to update the associated pitch or pulse state before the voice register writers run.
Decrements a per-slot delay, then fetches and masks the next pitch delta when the delay expires.
Adds a per-step increment to the modulator reload value or disables the slot and exits through the main iteration tail.
Updates the pitch offset for each active voice from its modulation stream. A counter times each step and the stream index advances by three, with a per-voice restart flag at its end.

Updates modulation and then runs the SID register writers for the active voices. For voice 1, the path at $F3D4 advances gate and duration counters, updates sustain, derives pulse width, and writes the frequency pair.
Advances the first voice's countdown and gate duty state and writes control, sustain, pulse width and frequency for that voice.
Applies the second voice's countdown and its control, sustain, pulse-width and frequency state to the second SID voice.
Applies the third voice's independent duration and waveform state to the third SID voice.
Low bytes of SID oscillator frequency words indexed by pitch.
High bytes matching the pitch indices in the low-byte table.
Fixed-width 32-byte records selected by effect number. The reader uses gate, timing, envelope, two modulation records, sustain increment and optional arpeggio data.
The records with indices $20 through $29 start in these pages. The title uses descriptor $22 for voice 2 and the completion code requests descriptor $28.
